title: Not good to be alone (Genesis 2:18–25)
hookLine: the first thing the Torah calls "not good" is loneliness

lines: A HUMAN, ALONE IN A GARDEN.
cards: So far, everything in this story has been good. Light, good. Land, good.
Sun and moon, fish and birds, good. At the end of the sixth day, very good: seven times, as you heard on day six. Then the human is alone in the garden.
Plenty to eat, nothing dangerous, nothing wrong, you'd think. And for the first time in the Torah, God looks at something and says it's not good. Not a sin.
Not a monster. Not a flood.

teach.b: In the Jewish Publication Society's 1917 translation: "It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a help meet for him." The first not good is loneliness.
That old phrase, help meet, is often heard as a helper, an assistant.

teach.h: EZER — THE WORD USED FOR GOD.
teach.b: The Hebrew is ezer kenegdo. Ezer means help, and the Bible also uses it for God: "My help cometh from the LORD," say the Psalms, in the same translation. It's not a junior word.
Kenegdo means opposite him, facing him; readers hear an equal in it, someone who can look you in the eye.

Rashi noticed it can also mean against him, and gave a wry answer: if you're worthy, a help; if not, someone who pushes back. Then the animals come. The human names each one, and none of them is the one.
The human sleeps, and a second person is made from the first, from the side, the text says.
And the first human speaks the Torah's first human words, almost a song: "This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh." The rabbis carried the idea far beyond marriage.
The Talmud tells of Honi, who slept for seventy years, woke, and found that nobody knew him anymore.

It closes his story with a saying people used: either companionship, or death. Friends, study partners, community, family. People need people, and the Torah says so at the start, before anything else goes wrong.

how: Jewish tradition treats companionship as a basic need: study is often done in pairs, called chavruta, many prayers are said in community, and visiting the sick is counted a mitzvah.

o: a help who faces you as an equal
a companion made from the animals

games.q: what's inside the verse — tap the pairs.
p: help, a word used of God

s: the first thing called "not good" in the Torah is a sin
it's loneliness: "it is not good that the man should be alone."
ezer, help, is a word the Bible also uses for God
"my help cometh from the LORD": the same word.
ezer kenegdo: a help facing you, as an equal.

games.q: kenegdo can mean "facing him" or "against him." you're Rashi. how do you read it?
o: if worthy, a help; if not, one who pushes back.
games.why: Rashi's wry answer: worthy, a help; unworthy, against you. both can be true of the same person.

practice: Who might be lonely right now? An older neighbor, a friend who moved away, a coworker who eats lunch alone, someone who went quiet in the group chat. Hold one of their faces in mind, and stay with them for a few slow breaths.

wordCard.voice: Ezer kenegdo: help that faces you as an equal. The first not good in the Torah, and the help that meets it.

orig.note: Hebrew: a help facing him, alongside him as an equal.

carryVoice: Your line: not good alone. People need people, from the very first pages. See you on day twenty-eight.
